rules.title: Effects declare dependencies and clean up
rules.what: Every useEffect has a dependency array, and an effect that fetches, subscribes or starts a timer returns a cleanup.
rules.why: An effect with no dependency array runs after every render; when it fetches, the render it causes runs it again - a loop invisible in the code and obvious in the network panel.
rules.how: useEffect(() => { const c = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: c.signal }); return () => c.abort(); }, [url]); prefer a data-fetching library that deduplicates requests.

patterns.note: Single-line effect without a dependency array; multi-line effects are not seen by this pattern.

verify.how: A render test counts network calls and asserts one fetch per dependency change; unmount aborts in-flight requests.

rules.title: Virtualise or paginate long lists
rules.what: Render only the visible part of long lists (virtualisation or pagination), with stable keys that identify items, not indexes.
rules.why: Ten thousand rows mean ten thousand DOM nodes for the twenty on screen: memory, layout and every later interaction pay for it, worst on low-end devices.
rules.how: react-window/@tanstack/react-virtual, server pagination; key={item.id}, never key={index} on reorderable lists.

patterns.note: List rendered with map; candidate only if the list is long and not virtualised.
Index used as key: items are rebuilt on insert/reorder.

verify.how: React Profiler or DOM node count on the largest realistic dataset stays bounded.

rules.title: Memoise what profiling proves hot
rules.what: Keep state local, hoist stable values, and add useMemo/useCallback/memo only where the Profiler shows avoidable re-renders.
rules.why: Inline objects and functions are new references at every render, defeating memoised children; blanket memoisation, though, adds cost and complexity for nothing.
rules.how: Move constants out of the component; colocate state; profile, then memoise the measured hot path.

patterns.note: Inline object prop; matters only if the child is memoised or the list is large.

verify.how: React Profiler capture before/after on the interaction concerned.

rules.title: Do not ship a client runtime for static content
rules.what: Render non-interactive content statically or on the server, and split routes and optional features into lazy chunks.
rules.why: A client-side runtime for content that never changes costs download, parse and hydration on every visit, and excludes slow devices and networks first.
rules.how: Static generation or server components for content; React.lazy + Suspense per route; measure JS per route.

verify.how: Bundle analysis shows per-route chunks; JS transferred on the content pages within budget.

rules.title: Evaluate a lighter runtime against a baseline
rules.what: When Preact (or another lighter runtime) is used or a migration is being evaluated, compare the production bundle and the essential interactions against the current baseline, with compatibility and accessibility checked; never migrate on reputation.
rules.why: A smaller runtime saves bytes on every visit only if the libraries and accessibility behaviour survive; a migration that breaks them costs more than it saves.
rules.how: Measure bundle and interaction timings before/after on the same build settings; run the accessibility checks; drop compatibility layers the target browsers do not need.

verify.how: Bundle size and interaction timings compared to the baseline; accessibility checks pass.
